I'm going to try and remember this as an example of why it's okay to ignore good advice sometimes.

As pointed out a few times upthread, this is a D&D creature translated into SCP. The only difference is that a Worm That Walks gets spell slots. But it's well-executed enough that I don't care, and a majority of voters would seem to agree.

Only nitpick I have is that the thing about getting two earthworms when you cut one in half is a myth. There is room in the article for that feature to stay, but it should at least get a footnote from the researcher that they recognize this isn't normal for roundworm species.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have three complains about this one that keep me from up-voting, and only its age keeps me from down-voting for now.

First, it could be easily far more clinical than it is now
example:

The first paragraph of description could cut out the "writhing" and simplify all the physical description for something like "it is a colony of invertebrates that resemble dark brown fly worms, or earthworms. Except for individuals taken out of the main mass, the colony behaves as a single organism".

"Acidic strength" could be exchanged for a specific pKa or pH value quickly searched on wikipedia, and if possible associated with another material (though highly corrosive on human skin, hydrofluoric acid is actually a weak acid that have an uncommon range of affected materials, including glass but excluding metals, and actually works as poison on us). Alternatively, it could be stated that the acid have a corrosive effect on human flesh similar to hydrofluoric acid.

In the same line, the velocity of corrosion could be presented as corrosion of mass/hour or something similar, unless it is supposed to corrode any quantity of anything under an hour.

Seriously, how attempting to remove it from a victim is fruitless? What this sentence wants to mean? Or disturbing it, by the way. Is it indifferent to harm even if suffering it? Is it immune to harm while feeding? Does it fixate to the victim to the point of resisting being removed? It just said nothing as it is written now, for complete lack of information.

The tenacity of it to reach prey, and ability to reroute, is too awkwardly described. Also, as it is an anomaly being described, it isn't necessary to repeatedly say that the means to achieve something isn't known. It wouldn't be an anomaly otherwise.

Most of the quoted words are precisely on parts where the author should be more clinical and seems to know it.

Danger level overrated
– hide block

We have an interesting piece here: it is a mass of worms that seems to have a hive-mind, but didn't gave enough data to confirm this. It is capable of intelligent hunting, have a marked preference for human meat, is able to mimic human speech and secrets a strong digestive acid.

But nothing that is shown actually makes it as dangerous to contain as it is treated. The containment cell needs to be airtight, but there seems to be no real need for four security cameras, just the same cautions needed for standard containment of worms.

There is no apparent need for it to be impossible to remove from prey, specially since some acids can poison a victim with short-term contact even if removed. The statements about how it hunts clearly focus more on saying that it is impossible to avoid than actually describing relevant information on its hunting techniques.

On the same vein, the speech mimicry is described in a manner that focus too much on saying how it is a clever predator, but ultimately it just say that at the end you'll be screwed. Does it identifies the best hiding locations? What are its preferred spots? It seems it is simply "always right and clever".

Finally, the last paragraph is too focused on defining how the creature could be destroyed, as if stating that it should be incredibly hard to achieve. It isn't, it is just as hard as killing an entire earthworm colony. Not only it seems out of place in an SCP document, nothing on the article actually makes this a relevant question. The only pieces of information actually relevant are that it will reproduce until it recovers its initial mass if needed, and that it can survive at a slowed metabolism just under 5ºC.

Finally, it lacks anything interesting actually going on.
It is a problem with such a lengthy article.

At several places, the article indicates that this thing is unnerving to interact with, and that there was some history to it or its acquisition. But for now, those allusions are just an excuse to say things without showing things.

This article could work nicely just describing the thing, if it was short. But as it is now, it is too long to not have a better pay-off. It could use some logs of the actual interactions, and subsequent notations.


For now, I'm really tempted to down-vote this article until it is improved in some way.

The worm that walks: the scp.
I like the core concept this was based on, but the execution seems… kinda basic. Doesn't really have a hook. One can argue the speech aspect is enough, doesn't really get to me though. Novoted.

And by the way, you don't get two earthworms when you cut one. You get one shorter but able to function and one butt that dies off quickly. They can heal but are unable to regenerate the whole head part. I know people commonly say this is a thing, but only sponges, echinoderms and some flatworms are able to regenerate like that. There, the angry biologist in my head is calmed for now.

item.content:encoded:
You know, I see what you're saying on the laughter, but I think the repeating someone's name (or stilted imitations of people in general) is definitely creepier. So that's good.

The "out there" ones just looked stupid when I put them in, and the more scientific ones either looked too implausible or took away from the horror.

Yeah, that's definitely understandable.

The worms are extremely simple, they have no teeth or claws, they can't exactly rip you to shreds, they need some way to attack, some way to break down their food and something they can use to get through most barriers.

The problem here is that the reason they have super acid is because the author needed them to. So it feels a little contrived. Though it's not impossible to pull off - I could buy it, and most other commenters already seem to. For me, it would need to have some in-universe logic or just be scarier (I can't really picture having nightmares about acid).

why it likes to eat people is up to the reader.

The problem with that is that if it's not interesting enough AND there's no explanation, a reader (such as me) may think the only reason it eats people is because the author wanted it to. Which makes it feel contrived; artificial; hurts suspension of disbelief. Your addendum showing that the SCP researchers wondered the same thing helps a bit (always a powerful tool to have characters ask the same questions as the reader), but for me at least, not quite enough.

But hey, YMMV, of course. It's like the old trope of dragons having hordes of treasure; some people (me!) can't stand that outside of Tolkien's works and D&D, because it doesn't make any goddamn sense for dragons to horde treasure outside those works - and other people are just fine with those dragons and their treasure, because they're so used to taking it for granted. Since I'm the minority opinion, I think, take it for what it's worth. =]

P.S. Why indeed? It's all part of the ~Mystery~

I lol'ed. =D

"Where did this creature come from? Was it biologically engineered to prefer eating people? Why? Is it some kind of elemental mythical beastie? I'm not saying you need to know the origin for this thing to make it a good SCP, but it feels a little weird as it is; the 'not sure if I buy it, sounds like a stretch' kind of weird instead of the 'holy crap how did that happen' kind of weird."

Well, in truth, I had a while batch of possible "origin" stories, everything from a mutated version of standard worms to an ancient blood god summoned by a druidic cult. But none of them really fit. The "out there" ones just looked stupid when I put them in, and the more scientific ones either looked too implausible or took away from the horror. In the end, I left the origin out - how it got here and why it likes to eat people is up to the reader.

item.content:encoded:
Drat, I knew I should have clarified that more.

Thinking about the origin was just a suggestion, which might help fix some of the stuff I whined about not making sense. Acid-spewing worms that shapeshift into people and also prey on people for no apparent reason aren't as interesting - to me - as acid-spewing worms that shapeshift into people and also prey on people because of X reason.

X reason could be '906 likes delicious brains, which humans have more of', anti-human biological weapon, supernatural beastie that preys on people as part of its purpose in some mythological world order… the possibilities are endless, really.

You don't even need an X reason - you could just have it be an equal-opportunity predator of other animals of sufficient size as well, with expanded shapeshifting capabilities to match - army ants can make themselves into living architecture of all kinds, why can't 906 take more than one form? (Now I'm imagining it as a twisted, shambling elephant, attempting trumpeting noises…)

Or a whole bunch of other options I haven't thought of.

But without some kind of connecting detail, 906 seems cut-and-pasted together. And some of those cut-and-paste parts (preying on humans, super acid) are too generic on their own.

None of this would apply to, say, 173, 682, or 914.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nitpick: "These organisms seem to interact in a uniform fashion, forming a colloquial "superorganism" in a similar manner to army ants."
They don't 'seem to' - they DO interact in a uniform fashion. This stands out to me because I make this mistake all the goddamn time. :)

Overall I like this - it's difficult not to, because goddamn the picture is good. Even so…

* Why the creepy laughter? Comes off a little cheesy.
* Why the combination of super acid and primarily targeting humanoids? Primarily targeting humanoids makes sense with the form it takes (which you don't wanna get rid of, I mean look at that picture), but why do you need super acid to eat people? For that matter, what are the odds that it has BOTH super acid AND eats people?
* Where did this creature come from? Was it biologically engineered to prefer eating people? Why? Is it some kind of elemental mythical beastie? I'm not saying you need to know the origin for this thing to make it a good SCP, but it feels a little weird as it is; the 'not sure if I buy it, sounds like a stretch' kind of weird instead of the 'holy crap how did that happen' kind of weird.

The humanoid form thing would also make sense if it tried to mimic the shape of any prey target it sees. Though I still don't know why it would focus on people primarily. The delicious brains? That would explain going for the pig next after the human… don't remember intelligence comparisons of the others, but maybe you could point that out as possibility. But then… if it's the brains they want, why dissolve the brains to undifferentiated slurry with super acid? Food for thought. (ha! …that was unintentional, I swear)

item.content:encoded:
"Testing of SCP-906 which involved placing a Class D and a cow into a testing chamber with SCP-906 resulted in SCP-906 targeting the Class D before the cow." (run on sentence)

Er, no, it's not. Awkward and unwieldy, maybe (I do think it might benefit from revision), but not a run-on and not inherently incorrect. The phrase "which involved placing a Class D and a cow into a testing chamber with SCP-906" is an adjectival phrase modifying "Testing." It can't stand on it's own, and if you take it out, you get "Testing of SCP-906 resulted in SCP-906 targeting the Class D before the cow," which is a perfectly valid sentence.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
More nitpicks:
-The phrase "a bipedal humanoid" is redundant. If it's not bipedal, it's not humanoid.
-Caustic and corrosive are not synonymous: caustic refers to the actions of strong bases, while corrosive refers to acids. So is their secretion acidic or basic? Also, titanium is already corrosion-resistant, so saying the secretion doesn't significantly affect Ti doesn't really say much. And, if it doesn't affect glass, then its effect is not comparable to hydrofluoric acid. (Also, what the heck is acid-treated glass? A Google search found that "acid-treated glass" was just made translucent, or had translucent patterns put in, via etching.)
-Whether the gunk is caustic or corrosive, either way it's not going to melt anything. The word you want is dissolve.
-If you cut an earthworm, all you'll get is a dead earthworm. You're thinking flatworms, not earthworms.

Too many little problems like this in the article. The concept itself seems okay, but downvoting on execution.

As of right now, I really dislike this. I think it's the writing — stylistically there are major issues. For example:

"This substance has been shown to destroy a full human being" (unscientific)
"acidic substance" (I would have written secretions instead of substance)
"Testing of SCP-906 which involved placing a Class D and a cow into a testing chamber with SCP-906 resulted in SCP-906 targeting the Class D before the cow." (run on sentence)
"SCP-906 reportedly "said" a supervising staff members name several times." (why is said in quotes? It's not evocative or scientific; also, you're missing a possessive apostrophe)

Downvoted, for now. I think you really need a fresh pair of eyes to help edit and tighten this up.

item.content:encoded:
OK this? This is worlds better than the original. Very much upvoted.

Two notes:

1) Even though we are using metric measurements, I think the general consensus is to use the American spelling "meters" as opposed to "metres"
2) For something that can mimic the relative size of a humanoid (roughly 6 feet tall), I think that your containment box should be larger than 1x1x1. That many worms would probably fill the box to the brim and present somewhat of a challenge at feeding time. And your container measurement should be three dimensional, list length, width and height.
